topic: Tensor support saturation for complete causal identification under structural zeros. For a finite acyclic SCM with one mutually independent finite latent root per bidirected-clique district, known graph and supplied realizable exact observational support S, characterize uniform identification of P_x(Y) over every same-law model on the relative interior of S. Prove that first-forbidden-prefix saturation yields the unique maximal Cartesian response support; recover supported district Q-signatures; show identification iff the target response indicator belongs to their tensor row span; compile success into one rational functional with denominators positive throughout the face, and compile failure into strictly positive rational same-support, same-law twins differing in the query. Derive multinomial influence-function inference on fixed epsilon-interiors and a support-scoped dosearch compiler. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: forbidden-prefix deletion, positive-prefix Q-factor telescoping, and tensor row-span separation were derived as a non-QE proof spine. Exact checks cover 165 realizable binary-IV masks with 134 identified and 190 negative queries, all 255 frontdoor supports with 336 identified and 144 negative queries, and 463 alternating-district support images plus 64 tensor queries; the intervention ledger rejects the diagonal-bow substitution and derives the five-cell IV identity. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: compile the product-preserving SAT-SID rules, including signed intermediate expressions, into the bounded tensor/Q-factor certificate language and independently verify the maximal-support proof and novelty against quasi-Markovian credal networks. EARLY KILL TEST: attack first-forbidden-prefix saturation, then require rejection of Y=X after do(X=1) in the diagonal bow and derivation of the five-cell IV formula through the identified do(Z=1) kernel. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/scm_supportface_complete_id.md.

open_problems.open_problem: For finite quasi-Markovian SCMs with a supplied realizable observational support face, is uniform identification on that face equivalent to membership of the intervention-response indicator in the tensor row span of support-restricted district Q-signatures?

source_refs.claim: Derives graphical positivity conditions for given identification formulas and discusses, but does not complete, a positivity-aware identification algorithm.
source_refs.author: Inwoo Hwang, Yesong Choe, Yeahoon Kwon, Sanghack Lee

source_refs.claim: Tests constrained identifiability through arithmetic-circuit invariant cuts and demonstrates identification gains under logical constraints, including zeros.
source_refs.author: Yizuo Chen, Adnan Darwiche

source_refs.claim: Shows that functional dependencies can create identification beyond ordinary do-calculus, subject to explicit positivity conditions.
source_refs.author: Yizuo Chen, Adnan Darwiche

source_refs.claim: Reports that state constraints alone do not improve identifiability, although they can do so when combined with context-specific or functional information.
source_refs.author: Yizuo Chen, Adnan Darwiche

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing positivity-aware work determines when particular formulas are licensed, while arithmetic-circuit methods certify invariance for particular constrained instances. Neither gives a law-uniform necessary-and-sufficient criterion over every distribution in the relative interior of an exact support face. Moreover, the reported insufficiency of state constraints alone creates a boundary that must be reconciled explicitly: the proof must identify what additional information is contributed by realizability, district independence, and same-law face quantification. The missing step is a complete finite representation of support-compatible district mechanisms followed by a proof that constancy on every same-law fiber is exactly tensor row-span membership.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sound-and-complete theorem constructing the supported district-signature matrix, proving identification iff the target response vector lies in its tensor row span, and translating membership into a rational observational functional and nonmembership into same-law countermodels.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing moves directly from failure of strict positivity to graph-sensitive conditions that license causal identification formulas.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Classical identification formulas rely on positivity -> observational laws may contain structural zeros -> formula-specific positivity checks do not give a complete face-wise decision rule -> characterize identification uniformly on the supplied support face

method_exemplars.technique: Compile an interventional query into an arithmetic circuit and prove observational invariance by finding invariant cuts after constraint-aware simplification.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Circuit invariance and tensor row-span membership are alternative finite certificates that a query is constant across structural parameterizations inducing one observational law.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate a finite quasi-Markovian SCM into a credal network by expressing observations as constraints on exogenous response-type probabilities and evaluate interventions over the compatible credal set.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired row-span criterion uses the same finite exogenous-response representation but seeks an analytic singleton characterization specialized to an observational support face.

method_exemplars.technique: Turn graph-derived identifying functionals into estimators and derive their influence functions, asymptotic linearity, and efficiency properties.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once row-span membership yields a rational identifying functional, this is the closest graph-native template for converting it into an estimator and limit theorem.

open_problems.open_problem: With one mutually independent finite latent root per bidirected-clique district, does first-forbidden-prefix deletion produce the unique maximal Cartesian response-type support compatible with every law in the relative interior of a realizable observational support face?

source_refs.claim: Provides a compact exact credal-network representation of quasi-Markovian SCMs but does not characterize support-face maximal response supports.
source_refs.author: Marco Zaffalon, Alessandro Antonucci, Rafael Cabañas

source_refs.claim: Reduces discrete SCMs without loss to finite deterministic response types and causal bounds to polynomial programs over independent latent probabilities.
source_refs.author: Guilherme Duarte, Noam Finkelstein, Dean Knox, Jonathan Mummolo, Ilya Shpitser
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Uses zero-aware arithmetic-circuit pruning to establish constrained identification but gives no query-independent maximal Cartesian response-support theorem.
source_refs.author: Yizuo Chen, Adnan Darwiche

open_problems.why_unsolved: A zero observational cell excludes products of district response-type masses rather than merely excluding individual types. Credal-network and polynomial-program formulations preserve these multiplicative compatibility constraints, while arithmetic-circuit pruning is query-specific. The unresolved global-extension step is to prove that deleting each type at its first topological prefix forcing a forbidden cell is both necessary and sufficient: every surviving district type must admit jointly strictly positive masses without recreating a forbidden cell. Existing formulations do not establish that sufficiency or uniqueness.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A maximal-support theorem proving first-forbidden-prefix deletion necessary and sufficient for a unique largest product of district response supports, or a finite counterexample specifying the first graph and support face where uniqueness or sufficiency fails.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames finite causal inference through exogenous response distributions and isolates quasi-Markovian models as a compactly representable class.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Finite-SCM observations constrain latent response probabilities -> quasi-Markovian structure yields a compact product representation -> exact structural zeros should shrink the admissible response space -> characterize the maximal response-support product induced by those zeros

method_exemplars.technique: Canonicalize discrete structural equations into response types and translate observational evidence plus latent independence into polynomial constraints, proving equivalence to the original SCM optimization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed saturation theorem asks exactly which canonical response types can retain positive mass under the polynomial constraints imposed by a fixed observational support.

method_exemplars.technique: Propagate zero constants through an arithmetic circuit and prune incompatible branches before testing an invariant cut.
method_exemplars.why_closest: First-forbidden-prefix deletion is a support-global analogue of zero pruning, requiring local circuit simplification to be upgraded into a query-independent maximality proof.

open_problems.open_problem: Whenever the support-restricted tensor row-span criterion fails, must there exist strictly positive rational latent-response distributions on the same Cartesian support that induce the same observational law but different intervention-query values?

source_refs.claim: Gives a complete identification algorithm and graphical nonidentification constructions for recursive semi-Markovian models under the ordinary unrestricted observational model.
source_refs.author: Ilya Shpitser, Judea Pearl

source_refs.claim: Confirms completeness of ID but shows that the commonly cited hedge failure criterion is incorrect as stated and requires a more careful characterization.
source_refs.author: Ilya Shpitser

source_refs.claim: Computes sharp causal ranges over compatible discrete SCMs using polynomial optimization but generally does not produce symbolic rational same-support witnesses.
source_refs.author: Guilherme Duarte, Noam Finkelstein, Dean Knox, Jonathan Mummolo, Ilya Shpitser
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Reads identification as a singleton credal-network query but does not construct interior rational two-model witnesses for every nonsingleton query.
source_refs.author: Marco Zaffalon, Alessandro Antonucci, Rafael Cabañas

open_problems.why_unsolved: Classical hedge countermodels need not preserve a prescribed observational zero pattern or assign positive mass to every allowed response type, while numerical credal or polynomial optimization can establish a nondegenerate range without returning exact symbolic witnesses. A row-space separator initially supplies a linear perturbation, but independent district roots map their probabilities to observations multiplicatively. The missing proof step is to lift that separator to a rational curve inside the positive product simplex while fixing every observational cell and preventing support changes.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A constructive separation theorem producing two rational, strictly positive, same-response-support SCM parameterizations with identical observational distributions and unequal target values for every failed row-span instance, or a minimal counterexample to rational interior witnessing.

writing_exemplar.why: It exemplifies the necessary care for completeness-side claims by preserving algorithmic completeness while repairing an overstrong failure characterization.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A complete identifier must explain both success and failure -> standard graphical witnesses can be insufficiently precise -> exact support faces impose stronger witness requirements than ordinary hedges -> characterize failure using explicit same-support interior twins

method_exemplars.technique: Construct observationally equivalent causal models from the graphical obstruction returned by recursive c-component decomposition.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result is the support-face analogue of the classical completeness construction, with added positivity, rationality, and support-preservation requirements.

method_exemplars.technique: Parameterize finite SCMs by independent categorical response-type probabilities and identify their causal ranges with a polynomial program.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This supplies the semialgebraic same-law fiber on which an interior rational pair must be constructed.

method_exemplars.technique: Map observational compatibility to a credal set and test identifiability by constancy of the causal query over that set.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Rational twins would be a symbolic strengthening of the two-compatible-model interpretation implicit in credal nonidentification.

open_problems.open_problem: Can do-search be extended to a sound-and-complete support-scoped compiler whose product-preserving rules remain valid with zero cells and signed intermediate expressions and whose successful derivations normalize to bounded tensor/Q-factor certificates?

source_refs.claim: Do-search is complete only for identification settings already completely characterized by do-calculus; more advanced settings require additional rules.
source_refs.author: Santtu Tikka, Antti Hyttinen, Juha Karvanen

source_refs.claim: Relates post-hoc positivity checks, do-calculus, Q-decomposition, and algorithmic conditions, and identifies positivity-aware algorithm design as a further direction.
source_refs.author: Inwoo Hwang, Yesong Choe, Yeahoon Kwon, Sanghack Lee

source_refs.claim: Shows ordinary do-calculus is incomplete under context-specific independences and supplies a sound automated calculus while establishing computational hardness.
source_refs.author: Santtu Tikka, Antti Hyttinen, Juha Karvanen

open_problems.why_unsolved: Do-search manipulates probability expressions using rules whose standard side conditions do not encode an exact support face, while positivity-aware work primarily certifies denominators in formulas obtained by other means. Structural zeros require rules that preserve products and domains before cancellation. Signed intermediate expressions are a separate obstacle because nonnegative Q-factor semantics no longer apply term by term. No cited compiler is complete for face-specific identification gains or returns a bounded tensor certificate checkable against a finite response-support model.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite support-indexed rule system and compiler with soundness and completeness for the specified finite SCM class, plus a normalization theorem mapping every successful signed derivation to a denominator-safe rational tensor/Q-factor certificate.

writing_exemplar.why: It presents automated identification as a search over a compact calculus while clearly separating soundness, known completeness domains, and rule-based extensions.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Graphical identification rules are powerful but cumbersome to apply manually -> rule search automates heterogeneous identification problems -> completeness is inherited only where the underlying calculus is complete -> add support-face rules and checkable certificates for structural-zero identification

method_exemplars.technique: Represent probability expressions as search states, apply do-calculus and probability transformations as edges, and prove every transformation rule sound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed compiler is explicitly a support-aware enrichment of this rule-search architecture.

method_exemplars.technique: Propagate positivity requirements backward through Q-decomposition and identifying formulas to derive sufficient denominator conditions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its positive-prefix reasoning is the closest published machinery for attaching support-validity side conditions to compiler steps.

method_exemplars.technique: Enrich do-calculus search states with context-specific distributions and relations, then prove the added rules sound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Exact support information is also context-dependent, so its state-enrichment and calculus-extension strategy is a direct precedent.

open_problems.open_problem: For a support-face causal query compiled as a rational function of multinomial cell probabilities, can one derive its face-tangent efficient influence function and uniformly valid inference over fixed epsilon-interiors while characterizing loss of regularity as support changes?

source_refs.claim: Derives influence-function estimators and efficiency results for a broad class of hidden-variable graphical functionals while noting that general ID outputs remain difficult to estimate.
source_refs.author: Rohit Bhattacharya, Razieh Nabi, Ilya Shpitser

source_refs.claim: Studies positivity conditions licensing graphical identification formulas but does not develop influence-function inference on lower-dimensional support faces.
source_refs.author: Inwoo Hwang, Yesong Choe, Yeahoon Kwon, Sanghack Lee

source_refs.claim: Develops efficiency theory and influence-function inference for incremental interventions that avoid conventional positivity failures by changing the intervention.
source_refs.author: Edward H. Kennedy
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing graph-native semiparametric theory covers important classes of standard identifying functionals, while positivity-violation work often changes the estimand to match observed treatment support. Here the original intervention query is retained and may become identifiable precisely because the observational distribution lies on a lower-dimensional structural-zero face. The tangent space must therefore exclude forbidden cells, derivatives must be taken along that face, and uniformity depends on every compiled denominator remaining bounded away from zero. The cited work does not combine these ingredients.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit face-tangent multinomial efficient influence function, an efficient plug-in or one-step estimator with uniform asymptotic normality and variance consistency on each fixed epsilon-interior, and a boundary sequence demonstrating nonregularity when a required denominator or support cell vanishes.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames inference as the missing bridge between graphical identification algorithms and practically usable estimators.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Graphical algorithms identify many hidden-variable causal effects -> their output functionals can be difficult to estimate -> influence-function constructions bridge identification and efficient inference -> extend that bridge to rational functionals defined only on structural-zero faces

method_exemplars.technique: Differentiate graph-derived identifying functionals, construct influence-function estimating equations, and prove asymptotic linearity and efficiency.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result applies the same identification-to-inference pipeline after replacing a full-support statistical model with a multinomial support-face model.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive an efficient influence function and asymptotically normal estimator while tracking how overlap and denominator behavior control regularity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its proof isolates the statistical role of positivity, although the support-face problem retains the deterministic intervention target instead of replacing it.

literature_map:
Shpitser and Pearl (2006, AAAI) give the classical complete ID algorithm for recursive semi-Markovian models under the ordinary graphical model.
Shpitser (2023, arXiv:2307.03750) confirms ID completeness but corrects an overstrong hedge failure criterion, showing that completeness-side witnesses require careful formulation.
Hwang, Choe, Kwon, and Lee (2024, ICML) systematize positivity conditions through post-hoc checks, do-calculus, Q-decomposition, and algorithmic analysis, and discuss positivity-aware identifier design.
Chen and Darwiche (2024, NeurIPS; arXiv:2403.04919) prove identification gains from functional dependencies under explicit positivity conditions.
Chen and Darwiche (2024, arXiv:2412.02869) formalize constrained identifiability using arithmetic-circuit invariant cuts and show that logical constraints can enable identification.
Chen and Darwiche (2025, arXiv:2510.16703) distinguish state-level from variable-level effects and report that state constraints alone do not improve identification, creating a direct boundary for support-face claims.
Tikka, Hyttinen, and Karvanen (2019, NeurIPS; arXiv:2009.09768) show ordinary do-calculus is incomplete with context-specific independences and provide a sound automated calculus; the decision problem is NP-hard.
Tikka, Hyttinen, and Karvanen (2021, JSS; arXiv:1902.01073) implement do-search and establish completeness only in settings already completely characterized by do-calculus.
Zaffalon, Antonucci, and Cabañas (2020, PGM; arXiv:2008.00463) map quasi-Markovian finite SCMs exactly to credal networks, yielding singleton values or sharp intervals but not analytic support-face criteria.
Duarte, Finkelstein, Knox, Mummolo, and Shpitser (2023, JASA; arXiv:2109.13471) reduce discrete SCM bounds to polynomial programs over canonical response types and independent latent probabilities.
The Duarte et al. formulation is exact but computational; it does not isolate a tensor row-span singleton criterion or symbolic same-support countermodels.
Bhattacharya, Nabi, and Shpitser (2022, JMLR; arXiv:2003.12659) connect hidden-variable graphical identification to influence-function and efficient estimation for substantial but restricted functional classes.
Kennedy (2019, JASA; arXiv:1704.00211) develops efficiency theory for incremental interventions that avoid ordinary positivity failures, contrasting with retaining a deterministic query identified through structural zeros.
The main tension is that zeros are treated as obstacles requiring positivity, logical constraints enabling special-case identification, or inputs to numerical optimization; no located paper gives a complete uniform theory on an exact support face.
No located work combines maximal Cartesian response-support saturation, supported district-Q tensor completeness, denominator-safe rational compilation, rational interior nonidentification twins, and face-tangent multinomial inference.
